The test image shows two pepper fruits with large, dark, sunken lesions covering much of the fruit surface. The lesions have concentric ring-like patterns, are very dark (nearly black), and appear sunken/wrinkled. No fuzzy mold growth visible. This looks like fruit rot disease.

Top candidates: Anthracnose, Phytophthora_Blight, Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers, Rhizopus_Soft_Rots.

Let me view reference images one at a time.
Anthracnose shows smaller, more circular sunken lesion. Test image has much larger, extensive dark lesions. Let me check Phytophthora_Blight.
The test image has Bugwood ID 1568070 and this Phytophthora reference has 1568066 - same series! Let me check another Phytophthora_Blight reference showing fruit symptoms.
This Phytophthora on tomato is less dark than test image. Let me check Rhizopus_Soft_Rots and Alternaria next.
Rhizopus shows microscopic fungal image - not matching. Let me check Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers.
Alternaria shows stem canker on seedling - not matching. Let me check the third Phytophthora_Blight image.
6 views used, 4 classes covered. Need 2 more views on new classes. Let me check Gray_Mold and Sclerotinia.
Gray Mold shows cracked fruit with fuzzy white mold - doesn't match. Final view on Sclerotinia.

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Two pepper fruits with massive dark (near-black), sunken, wrinkled lesions covering most of the fruit surface. Some concentric patterning visible.
- **Anthracnose** (Bugwood_13): Shows smaller, circular sunken lesion - less extensive than test image.
- **Phytophthora_Blight** (Bugwood_100, 153, 21): Shows field wilting and stem lesions on pepper. The Bugwood ID of the test image (1568070) is adjacent to reference 1568066 (Phytophthora_Blight), strongly suggesting same collection. Phytophthora capsici causes large, dark, water-soaked fruit rot on peppers that turns nearly black.
- **Rhizopus_Soft_Rots**: Microscopic image, no match.
- **Alternaria**: Stem canker on seedling, no match.
- **Gray_Mold**: Cracked fruit with fuzzy white mold, no match.
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**: Wilting plant, no match.

The large, extensively dark, collapsed lesions on pepper fruit, combined with the Bugwood series adjacency, strongly point to **Phytophthora_Blight**. Phytophthora capsici fruit rot on peppers is known to produce exactly this type of large, dark, sunken lesion that can collapse the entire side of a fruit.
